text:
The newest pipelines don't end in a dashboard. They feed an AI assistant, which can only answer from what's in its index. Extract, clean, split, embed, index, keep fresh, delete. The fundamentals carry over. What's new is the vector store, and the embedding bill. Eleven questions, and every one gets worked through.

Question one. How have Data Engineer interviews changed with AI? The core hasn't: sequel, modeling, and batch and streaming design. On top: system design for AI data. Unstructured data, PDFs and tickets parsed into clean text. Vector search trade-offs. And AI in your own workflow. Some coding rounds allow an assistant, and grade how you check its code: idempotency, partition overwrites, time zones, schema drift. Now the pipeline itself.

Question two. Walk through the ingestion pipeline for a RAG assistant. RAG is retrieval-augmented generation: find the passages, then answer from them. Two halves. Offline, a pipeline builds the index. Online, each question is embedded, searched with a filter, reranked, and the best hits fill the prompt. Most of the work is offline. Extract incrementally, with change data capture or an updated-at watermark. Parse and clean: strip boilerplate, keep headings and tables, drop duplicates. Chunk, then attach metadata to each chunk: document id, section, timestamps, and who may read it. That makes filters, citations and deletes possible. Last, embed and upsert, keyed by a stable chunk id, so a retried batch overwrites instead of duplicating.
